planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in spring after last frost in well-drained soil in full sun; Nichols is a Louisiana-developed fig selection valued for good cold hardiness and reliable production in Gulf South dooryard plantings.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun. Nichols is a fig selection developed in Louisiana and long grown across the Gulf South for its reliable production of medium-large, brown-skinned figs with sweet, amber-pink flesh, along with good cold hardiness that lets it recover well after occasional hard freezes common at the northern edge of fig-growing country. Like other figs it fruits on both old and new wood, giving an early breba crop in late spring followed by a heavier main crop in late summer, and needs minimal care once established beyond an annual mulch layer and light pruning to manage size. Established plants regrow readily from the base if winter cold kills back the top growth in an unusually harsh year.

common_name: Improved Brown Turkey Fig (Larger-Fruited Brown Turkey Selection)

planting.note: Plant after the last hard frost in well-drained soil in full sun; Improved Brown Turkey is a selection valued for producing somewhat larger fruit than standard Brown Turkey while retaining the same reliable cold hardiness and heavy production.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun. Improved Brown Turkey is a selection of the classic Brown Turkey fig valued for producing somewhat larger, bronze-brown fruit with sweet, amber-pink flesh compared to standard Brown Turkey, while keeping the same dependable cold hardiness and heavy, reliable production that has made Brown Turkey one of the most widely planted figs in home gardens. Like other figs it bears on both old and new wood, giving an early breba crop in late spring followed by the main crop in late summer, and it needs minimal care beyond routine mulching and occasional pruning to control size. In colder zones, grow in a container that can be moved to shelter for winter.

common_name: Shasta Doublefile Viburnum (Compact Horizontal-Branching Flowering Viburnum)

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped shrubs in late winter or early spring in moist, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; Shasta is a compact doublefile viburnum selection with an especially heavy show of horizontally tiered white flower clusters in spring.

directions: Plant in moist, slightly acidic to neutral, well-drained soil in partial shade; doublefile viburnum blooms on the previous year's wood and should be pruned, if needed, only right after flowering. Shasta is a compact, wide-spreading selection of doublefile viburnum, producing an exceptionally heavy display of pure white, flat-topped lacecap flower clusters held in tiers along strongly horizontal branches in spring, followed by red berries that ripen to black and attract birds, and burgundy-red fall foliage color. Its strikingly tiered, horizontal branching habit gives the shrub a distinctive architectural presence even out of bloom, and it spreads noticeably wider than it grows tall, so allow ample lateral space when siting it.
